records.originalText: According to the TV, it will be fine today.
records.finalText: According to the weather forecast on TV, it will be fine today.
records.rationale: Specify the weather forecast rather than attributing speech to the TV apparatus; the same fine-weather prediction remains.

records.originalText: It is true that television also has some disadvantages.
records.finalText: It is true that television also has some disadvantages.
records.rationale: Also and it is true refer to an absent argument, while the disadvantages are not identified.

records.originalText: Speaking of television, what is your favorite show nowadays?
records.finalText: Speaking of television, what is your favorite show nowadays?
records.rationale: Speaking of television introduces a complete current-preference question without asserting a changing fact.

records.originalText: It is a pleasure to watch a baseball game on TV.
records.finalText: It is a pleasure to watch a baseball game on TV.
records.rationale: It is a pleasure expresses a subjective enjoyment of a clearly specified viewing activity.

records.originalText: The company is promoting a new car on TV.
records.finalText: The company is promoting a new car on TV.
records.rationale: Promoting a new car on TV describes a specific company's advertising activity naturally.

records.originalText: Even a small sound from the TV interferes with my concentration.
records.finalText: Even a small sound from the TV interferes with my concentration.
records.rationale: Interferes with my concentration is a natural personal observation with an explicit sound source.

records.originalText: Please show me the TV Guide.
records.finalText: Please show me the TV Guide.
records.rationale: The polite request names the TV Guide publication and forms complete direct speech.

records.originalText: The TV was so noisy that I couldn't concentrate on my reading.
records.finalText: The TV was so noisy that I couldn't concentrate on my reading.
records.rationale: Repeats 39265's television-noise interference with concentration, adding only a reading activity and past framing.

records.originalText: But I can't understand them very well.
records.finalText: But I can't understand them very well.
records.rationale: But and them have no discourse or object anchors in this standalone sentence.

records.originalText: But Dad won't like it.
records.finalText: But Dad won't like it.
records.rationale: The sentence depends on an absent contrast and it does not identify what Dad dislikes.

records.originalText: Secret police moved among the crowd during the demonstration.
records.finalText: Secret police moved among the crowd during the demonstration.
records.rationale: Moved among the crowd is natural narrative language about a specific demonstration, without endorsing surveillance.

records.originalText: I'm going to join a demonstration.
records.finalText: I'm going to join a demonstration.
records.rationale: Going to join a demonstration is a complete personal plan without a changing public-event assertion.

records.originalText: But what will you do if he doesn't come?
records.finalText: But what will you do if he doesn't come?
records.rationale: The question and first conditional are complete; initial but is valid conversational coordination.

records.originalText: But of course that was a long time ago.
records.finalText: But of course that was a long time ago.
records.rationale: But of course that refers to an entirely missing event and time comparison.

records.originalText: Shall we start the meeting now?
records.finalText: Shall we start the meeting now?
records.rationale: Shall we start the meeting now is a natural complete joint-action proposal.

records.originalText: The department store was crammed with holiday shoppers.
records.finalText: The department store was crammed with holiday shoppers.
records.rationale: Crammed with holiday shoppers is a natural bounded description of a crowded store.

records.originalText: Department stores sell numerous things.
records.finalText: Department stores sell numerous things.
records.rationale: The broad retail definition is stable, elementary and appropriately modest about merchandise variety.

records.originalText: You can see the large exhibition at the department store anytime.
records.finalText: You can see the large exhibition at the department store anytime.
records.rationale: Anytime makes an unrestricted availability promise without exhibition dates or opening-hour context.

records.originalText: A very pleasant young woman waited on me in the department store.
records.finalText: A very pleasant young woman waited on me in the department store.
records.rationale: Waited on me is a valid service phrasal verb within a specific past department-store encounter.

records.originalText: Let's see if I've got that right.
records.finalText: Let's see if I've got that right.

records.originalText: I'd like to pay with my credit card instead.
records.finalText: I'd like to pay with my credit card instead.
records.rationale: Pay with my credit card is complete ordinary purchase speech; instead marks an implicit payment alternative.

records.originalText: Some boys play tennis and others play soccer.
records.finalText: Some boys play tennis and others play soccer.

records.originalText: Playing tennis is good for your health.
records.finalText: Playing tennis is good for your health.
records.rationale: The unqualified health-benefit instruction lane needs more activity and individual suitability context than the source supplies.

records.originalText: Such sports as tennis and baseball are very popular.
records.finalText: Such sports as tennis and baseball are very popular.
records.rationale: Very popular has no population or period, making the sport-popularity assertion unbounded.

records.originalText: Tennis is difficult. I never know which way the ball is going to fly.
records.finalText: Tennis is difficult. I never know which way the ball is going to fly.
records.rationale: The difficulty assessment is explicitly personal and the ball-direction clause explains it naturally.

records.originalText: When it comes to tennis, she is second to none.
records.finalText: When it comes to tennis, she is second to none.
records.rationale: When it comes to and second to none are conventional idioms in a situated skill assessment.

records.originalText: I'll take you on at tennis.
records.finalText: I'll take you on at tennis.

records.originalText: He is no match for me in tennis.
records.finalText: He is no match for me in tennis.

records.originalText: I am no match for you at tennis.
records.finalText: I am no match for you at tennis.

records.originalText: Detroit is famous for its car industry.
records.finalText: Detroit is famous for its car industry.

records.originalText: I didn't do well on the test so my parents chewed me out.
records.finalText: I didn't do well on the test so my parents chewed me out.

records.originalText: I'm concerned about the result of the exam.

records.originalText: Please refrain from pushing forward.
records.finalText: Please refrain from pushing forward.

records.originalText: Running as fast as she could, she still failed to catch the bus.
records.finalText: Running as fast as she could, she still failed to catch the bus.

records.originalText: I'll meet him at the earliest opportunity possible.
records.finalText: I'll meet him at the earliest opportunity.

records.originalText: Make it as spicy as you can.
records.finalText: Make it as spicy as you can.

records.originalText: Try to jump as high as possible.
records.finalText: Try to jump as high as possible.

records.originalText: Don't use slang if you can help it.
records.finalText: Don't use slang if you can help it.

records.originalText: Enjoy life while you may.
records.finalText: Enjoy life while you may.

records.originalText: Well done! Your parents must be proud of you.
records.finalText: Well done! Your parents must be proud of you.

records.originalText: Put the tables end to end.

records.originalText: Table manners vary from one country to another.
records.finalText: Table manners vary from one country to another.

records.originalText: The table was covered with dust.
records.finalText: The table was covered with dust.

records.originalText: There was a lamp hanging above the table.
records.finalText: There was a lamp hanging above the table.

records.originalText: The legs of the table are shaky.
records.finalText: The legs of the table are shaky.

records.originalText: Don't put the glass near the edge of the table.
records.finalText: Don't put the glass near the edge of the table.

records.originalText: Inhaling diesel exhaust is bad for our health.
records.finalText: Inhaling diesel exhaust is bad for our health.

records.originalText: Each person was given enough food and clothing.
records.finalText: Each person was given enough food and clothing.

records.originalText: A foolish misunderstanding severed their long friendship.
records.finalText: A foolish misunderstanding severed their long friendship.

records.originalText: Don't waste your time on trifles.

records.originalText: I met your father just now.

records.originalText: At last, I caught up with my friends.
records.finalText: At last, I caught up with my friends.

records.finalText: The rebel was ultimately captured and confined to jail.

records.originalText: I guess the time of reckoning has arrived at last.

records.originalText: Now you've given yourself away.
records.finalText: Now you've given yourself away.

records.originalText: At last, my wish has come true.
records.finalText: At last, my wish has come true.

records.originalText: At last, we got to the lake.

records.originalText: At last, it began to rain.
records.finalText: At last, it began to rain.

records.originalText: He finally decided to go to his mother with the news his father had shared.
records.finalText: He finally decided to go to his mother with the news his father had shared.

records.originalText: Finally, he gave in to my persuasion.
records.finalText: Finally, he gave in to my persuasion.

records.finalText: Eventually, he was sentenced to five years in prison for the violent crime.

records.originalText: A foolish impulse made me say what I should have left unsaid.
records.finalText: A foolish impulse made me say what I should have left unsaid.

records.originalText: Why don't you give your mouth a rest?
records.finalText: Why don't you give your mouth a rest?

records.originalText: There was a slight chill in the air.
records.finalText: There was a slight chill in the air.

records.originalText: Discussion resumed after a short interruption.
records.finalText: Discussion resumed after a short interruption.
records.rationale: Resumed after a short interruption is a natural collocation describing a specific discussion sequence.

records.originalText: Now just hold on a minute.
records.finalText: Now just hold on a minute.
records.rationale: Hold on a minute is a conventional complete request to pause in direct speech.

records.originalText: I'm just going to run down to buy some tickets.
records.finalText: I'm just going to run down to buy some tickets.

records.originalText: If you stop and relax, this will relieve the tension and stress in your shoulders.
records.finalText: If you stop and relax, this will relieve the tension and stress in your shoulders.

records.finalText: Why don't we break off for a while and have some coffee?

records.originalText: I'll drop if I don't sit down.
records.finalText: I'll drop if I don't sit down.

records.originalText: I'm just going across to the flower shop.
records.finalText: I'm just going across to the flower shop.

records.originalText: Let me say a few words by way of apology.
records.finalText: Let me say a few words by way of apology.

records.originalText: I really spoke too harshly.
records.finalText: I really spoke too harshly.

records.originalText: A mere glance is not enough for us to tell one from the other.
records.finalText: A mere glance is not enough for us to tell one from the other.

records.originalText: Won't you come in for a moment?

records.originalText: Do you want to look into it?

records.originalText: A slip of tongue will often lead us to unexpected results.
records.finalText: A slip of the tongue will often lead us to unexpected results.

records.originalText: It's a shot in the arm.

records.originalText: Please take the pants in a bit.

records.originalText: I've been thinking that I may have been too critical.
records.finalText: I've been thinking that I may have been too critical.

records.originalText: I'd like to speak to you for a moment.

records.originalText: We have just cleaned the lavatory.

records.originalText: Team members are provided with equipment and uniforms.

records.originalText: It happened that I sat next to her at a meeting.
records.finalText: It happened that I sat next to her at a meeting.
records.rationale: Repeats 40557's coincidental encounter with the same woman, changing only the meeting setting and seat proximity.

records.originalText: Just take my word for it.
records.finalText: Just take my word for it.
records.rationale: Take my word for it is a conventional complete request to trust the speaker's assurance.

records.originalText: It is possible that he may know the fact.
records.finalText: It is possible that he may know the fact.
records.rationale: Possible that he may duplicates the uncertainty and the fact itself has no content referent.

records.originalText: He may well be right.
records.finalText: He may well be right.
records.rationale: May well be right is a natural graded epistemic assessment in direct speech.

records.originalText: Possibly, the accident will delay his arrival.
records.finalText: Possibly, the accident will delay his arrival.
records.rationale: Possibly explicitly marks an uncertain delay prediction caused by a particular accident.

records.originalText: I guess that's just the way the cookie crumbles.
records.finalText: I guess that's just the way the cookie crumbles.
records.rationale: Semantic repeat of the published that-is-the-way-the-ball-bounces acceptance idiom, expressed through a different metaphor.

records.originalText: In all probability, the cabinet will fall.
records.finalText: In all probability, the cabinet will fall.
records.rationale: The cabinet-collapse prediction has no country or period and risks being mistaken for a current political claim.

records.originalText: In all probability, the money will not be paid.
records.finalText: In all probability, the money will not be paid.
records.rationale: In all probability clearly marks a speaker's uncertain prediction about a particular payment.

records.originalText: I'd like a double room.
records.finalText: I'd like a double room.
records.rationale: Repeats the published I-would-like-to-book-a-double-room request with book omitted.

records.originalText: Loose jackets are the latest fad.
records.finalText: Loose jackets are the latest fad.
records.rationale: The latest-fad assertion lacks place and date and cannot be verified from the sentence pin.

records.originalText: Put out your cigarette. Smoking's not permitted here.
records.finalText: Put out your cigarette. Smoking's not permitted here.
records.rationale: The cigarette-extinguishing request and stated local prohibition form coherent direct speech, not a universal law claim.

records.originalText: I don't mind if you smoke.
records.finalText: I don't mind if you smoke.
records.rationale: Don't mind if naturally expresses a particular speaker's permission; it makes no health-benefit claim.

records.originalText: Let me have a cigarette.
records.finalText: Let me have a cigarette.
records.rationale: The bare cigarette request offers little general learning value while presenting tobacco uptake without context.

records.originalText: It goes without saying that smoking is bad for the health.
records.finalText: It goes without saying that smoking is bad for the health.
records.rationale: The unqualified health statement and goes-without-saying framing do not supply a scoped factual review.

records.originalText: Smoking is bad for your health.
records.finalText: Smoking is bad for your health.
records.rationale: The general smoking-health claim belongs in a separately fact-reviewed health context rather than source-only publication.

records.originalText: Excessive smoking will injure your health.
records.finalText: Excessive smoking will injure your health.
records.rationale: The health prediction uses an undefined excessive threshold and lacks the scoped review required for this subject.

records.originalText: A new tax has been imposed on cigarettes.
records.finalText: A new tax has been imposed on cigarettes.
records.rationale: The asserted new cigarette tax has no jurisdiction or effective date and is time-dependent.

records.originalText: Even if you are busy, you should keep your promise.
records.finalText: Even if you are busy, you should keep your promise.
records.rationale: Even if and should express a coherent personal obligation despite a busy schedule.

records.originalText: Even if he is busy, he will come.
records.finalText: Even if he is busy, he will come.
records.rationale: Even if he is busy introduces a clear conditional attendance prediction about one person.

records.originalText: No matter what he says, I'll never believe him again.
records.finalText: No matter what he says, I'll never believe him again.
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the published I-will-never-trust-Tom-again statement; the speech concession supplies only emphasis.

records.originalText: Even if you have your own way, you will not always be successful.
records.finalText: Even if you have your own way, you will not always be successful.
records.rationale: Have your own way is a natural idiom inside a qualified success prediction, not a guaranteed universal outcome.

records.originalText: You have another chance even if you fail this time.
records.finalText: You have another chance even if you fail this time.
records.rationale: Another chance even if you fail is a complete encouragement about a specific attempt.

records.originalText: Even if you stop me, I won't change my mind.
records.finalText: Even if you stop me, I won't change my mind.
records.rationale: Repeats the existing refusal-to-change-one's-mind proposition, adding only a hypothetical attempt to stop the speaker.

records.originalText: Even if I have to sell my house, I'll keep my business going.
records.finalText: Even if I have to sell my house, I'll keep my business going.
records.rationale: Even if I have to sell my house expresses a personal extreme contingency and business commitment, without recommending it to others.

records.originalText: Even though it is raining, he will play golf.
records.finalText: Even though it is raining, he will play golf.
records.rationale: Even though marks actual rain and a specific personal golf plan naturally.

records.originalText: Even if it rains, the game will be played.
records.finalText: Even if it rains, the game will be played.
records.rationale: Even if it rains and the future passive express a coherent conditional game-scheduling statement.

records.originalText: The game will be played even if it rains.
records.finalText: The game will be played even if it rains.
records.rationale: Exactly the same game-in-rain proposition as 40763 with only clause order changed.

records.originalText: The soccer game will be played, even if it rains.
records.finalText: The soccer game will be played, even if it rains.
records.rationale: Repeats 40763's rain-despite-game scheduling statement, adding only soccer and a comma.

records.originalText: Even if you are not to blame, you should apologize.
records.finalText: Even if you are not to blame, you should apologize.
records.rationale: The unconditional apology advice lacks the social situation needed to judge responsibility and appropriateness.

records.originalText: Whichever you choose, you cannot lose.
records.finalText: Whichever you choose, you cannot lose.
records.rationale: Whichever you choose supplies no options and cannot lose is an unsupported unconditional assurance.

records.originalText: There are few, if any, such men.
records.finalText: There are few, if any, such men.
records.rationale: Such men lacks the defining description and leaves the few-if-any claim without a subject category.

records.originalText: You must do the work, even if you do not like it.
records.finalText: You must do the work, even if you do not like it.
records.rationale: The direct work obligation and even-if dislike clause form a complete ordinary task instruction.

records.originalText: Whenever you visit him, you will find him playing video games.
records.finalText: Whenever you visit him, you will find him playing video games.
records.rationale: Whenever frames the described person's recurring gaming habit, not a general population claim.

records.originalText: The millionaire insisted on acquiring the masterpiece no matter how much it cost.
records.finalText: The millionaire insisted on acquiring the masterpiece no matter how much it cost.
records.rationale: Insisted on acquiring correctly takes a gerund and no-matter-how-much supplies a coherent cost concession.

records.originalText: Even if you go far away, let's keep in touch with each other over the phone.
records.finalText: Even if you go far away, let's keep in touch with each other over the phone.
records.rationale: Repeats the travel-despite-regular-contact proposition already retained in 38035, varying distance and mutuality.

records.originalText: Even if it takes you three years, you must accomplish your goal.
records.finalText: Even if it takes you three years, you must accomplish your goal.
records.rationale: Even if it takes three years qualifies a specific goal obligation in grammatical direct speech.

records.originalText: There is no accounting for tastes.
records.finalText: There is no accounting for tastes.
records.rationale: No accounting for tastes is an established idiom expressing acceptance of different preferences.

records.originalText: The lights went out just now.
records.finalText: The lights went out just now.
records.rationale: Repeats the already-published lights-went-out event while dropping its reading-interruption context.

records.originalText: All you have to do is to cultivate the ability to put yourself in the other fellow's place.
records.finalText: All you have to do is to cultivate the ability to put yourself in the other fellow's place.
records.rationale: Put yourself in another's place is a valid empathy idiom; cultivate the ability is natural formal wording.

records.originalText: She left me simply because I had a small income.
records.finalText: She left me simply because I had a small income.
records.rationale: Simply because connects a particular separation with the speaker's attributed income-related reason.

records.originalText: The only solution is for her to give up the plan.
records.finalText: The only solution is for her to give up the plan.
records.rationale: For her to give up correctly complements solution in a situated speaker assessment.

records.originalText: How about giving me a promotion from just-a-friend to boyfriend?
records.finalText: How about giving me a promotion from just-a-friend to boyfriend?
records.rationale: The promotion metaphor is understandable playful romantic speech with explicit starting and desired relationship roles.

records.originalText: It was bad enough that he usually came to work late, but coming in drunk was the last straw, and I'm going to have to let him go.
records.finalText: It was bad enough that he usually came to work late, but coming in drunk was the last straw, and I'm going to have to let him go.
records.rationale: The linked past habits, last-straw idiom and present employment decision form a coherent complex utterance.

records.originalText: All that I was looking for was somebody who looked like you.
records.finalText: All that I was looking for was somebody who looked like you.
records.rationale: The all-that cleft-like emphasis and looked-like relative clause are grammatical and coherent.

records.originalText: He lost his position just because he refused to tell a lie.
records.finalText: He lost his position just because he refused to tell a lie.
records.rationale: The refusal-to-lie reason clause naturally explains a specific job-loss event.

records.originalText: It was careless of you to leave your umbrella in the taxi.
records.finalText: It was careless of you to leave your umbrella in the taxi.
records.rationale: Careless of you to leave correctly frames a particular forgotten-umbrella incident.

records.originalText: Let's go by taxi, shall we?
records.finalText: Let's go by taxi, shall we?
records.rationale: Let's plus shall-we tag is a natural shared taxi-travel proposal.

records.originalText: A host of friends came to see me off.
records.finalText: A host of friends came to see me off.
records.rationale: A host of friends and see me off are valid expressions in a specific farewell event.

records.originalText: A lot of treasure was brought over to this country.
records.finalText: A lot of treasure was brought over to this country.
records.rationale: The passive treasure-transport account is complete narrative language, with no claim of verified historical origin.

records.originalText: Many birds are on the branch.
records.finalText: Many birds are on the branch.
records.rationale: The birds-on-a-branch description uses basic quantity and location grammar naturally.

records.originalText: Many boats are sailing on the sea.
records.finalText: Many boats are sailing on the sea.
records.rationale: The present continuous and sailing-on-the-sea phrase form a complete visible scene.

records.originalText: A bunch of people thrust their way toward the rear exit.
records.finalText: A bunch of people thrust their way toward the rear exit.
records.rationale: Thrust their way toward the rear exit is a natural advanced movement description of a specific crowd.

records.originalText: A number of people die in traffic accidents.
records.finalText: A number of people die in traffic accidents.
records.rationale: The mortality statement has no location, period or supporting figures and belongs in a scoped factual context.

records.originalText: He saw something behind a lot of old boxes.
records.finalText: He saw something behind a lot of old boxes.
records.rationale: Behind a lot of old boxes supplies a concrete spatial complement to a specific observation.

records.originalText: A lot of policemen guarded the hall.
records.finalText: A lot of policemen guarded the hall.
records.rationale: The police-guarded-hall statement is a clear specific past security event.

records.originalText: Dozens of students gathered there.
records.finalText: Dozens of students gathered there.
records.rationale: There supplies no gathering location and the sentence contributes little independent content beyond a vague group count.

records.originalText: Although he had many toys, his greed made him want more.
records.finalText: Although he had many toys, his greed made him want more.
records.rationale: Although introduces a coherent specific contrast between many toys and a child's desire for more.

records.originalText: Pigeons can find their way home with the help of the Earth's magnetic field.
records.finalText: Pigeons can find their way home with the help of the Earth's magnetic field.
records.rationale: The biological navigation mechanism needs scientific source review beyond the experimental sentence rating.

records.originalText: Not that I have any objection.
records.finalText: Not that I have any objection.
records.rationale: Not that is a discourse fragment depending entirely on an unstated proposal or preceding claim.

records.originalText: The word downtown refers to the business quarter of any town.
records.finalText: The word downtown refers to the business quarter of any town.
records.rationale: The downtown definition overgeneralizes to any town and needs regional and urban-geographic qualification.

records.originalText: Direct marketing is a means of allowing people to shop from home.
records.finalText: Direct marketing is a means of allowing people to shop from home.
records.rationale: Direct marketing and means of allowing form a grammatical, modest description of a shopping channel's capability.

records.originalText: Diamonds are a girl's best friends.
records.finalText: Diamonds are a girl's best friends.
records.rationale: The diamond maxim is an unframed gender stereotype and unattributed cultural slogan.
